explanation: A database organizes related data so it can be stored, searched, updated, and protected. A relational database uses tables: each row is a record and each column describes an attribute. introduction: This beginner lesson develops COUNT; SUM; AVG; MIN; MAX; NULL values. Use the isolated practice database to explore the example before writing your own activity.
explanation: Aggregates summarize several rows into one result. COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) counts non-NULL values. SUM totals, AVG computes the mean of known numeric values, and MIN/MAX find extremes. Most aggregates ignore NULL values; SUM or AVG of no matching values can be NULL, while COUNT returns zero. A missing average must not silently become a zero grade. Use ROUND only when presenting a value, and document what your statistic includes.

explanation: Window functions calculate over related rows while keeping individual rows visible.
